diagnosis.symptom: On iPhone 13 viewport (390x844) at /signup, a newly created user's onboarding dialog renders with its content and action row overflowing horizontally beyond the viewport.
diagnosis.likelyRootCause: The onboarding dialog in src/containers/UserOnboardingContainer.tsx (top candidate, matching captured DOM data-test hooks) likely uses a fixed width or non-responsive layout for its content/action row (e.g., a fixed min-width, large padding, or a Dialog/Button row without flex-wrap or max-width: 100%), causing horizontal overflow at narrow mobile widths.
diagnosis.patchHypothesis: Constrain the dialog within the viewport by setting a responsive max-width (e.g., maxWidth="xs" or width: 100% with boxSizing) on the Dialog/Paper, and allow the action row to wrap (flex-wrap: wrap) or shrink (min-width: 0) inside UserOnboardingContainer.tsx, so both the content text and DialogActions buttons fit within 390px.
verificationPlan: Reload /signup at 390x844 as a new user and confirm the onboarding dialog is fully visible with no horizontal scroll.
Check that document.scrollingElement.scrollWidth <= viewport width while the dialog is open.
Verify the action row buttons remain tappable and wrap rather than clipping.
Re-run at a wider viewport (e.g., 1280px) to confirm no regression in desktop layout.
Inspect verify.json/patch.diff outputs to confirm the change is scoped to UserOnboardingContainer.tsx.
residualRisks: Other dialogs sharing the same Dialog/Paper styles could be affected if global styles are changed instead of local ones.
Wrapping the action row may alter button order/visual hierarchy on small screens.
Console errors (6) and xstate transient-transition warnings are unrelated here but may mask other onboarding state issues.
Screenshot alone cannot confirm exact overflow source; runtime inspection of computed styles is needed.
Fix may not address overflow if it originates from a child component (e.g., TransactionItem) embedded in the dialog.
